cse-2021-1-ga-4.approach: Every punch made on a fold line is a half-hole that doubles across that fold when unfolded; undo the folds in reverse order and mirror each hole.

steps.title: Read the folded state
steps.body: Fold 1: right half onto left (vertical crease). Fold 2: lower half up (horizontal crease). The final piece is the top-left quarter, with the vertical crease on its right edge and the horizontal crease on its bottom edge. Punches: a wide, short rectangle on the vertical crease near the top; a small square on the horizontal crease; a quarter-circle at the centre corner.

steps.title: Undo fold 2 (horizontal crease)
steps.body: The square on the horizontal crease doubles vertically into a small **tall** slot on the left. The rectangle (above the crease) is mirrored to a second rectangle below. The quarter-circle becomes a semicircle.

steps.title: Undo fold 1 (vertical crease)
steps.body: The rectangles sit on the vertical crease, so each doubles horizontally into a **wide horizontal** slot, one at top and one at bottom. The tall slot on the left is mirrored to the right. The semicircle becomes a full centre circle.

steps.title: Match
steps.body: Result: centre hole, wide horizontal slots at top and bottom, small upright slots left and right — option (A).

optionAnalysis.reason: Matches: wide horizontal slots top/bottom (from the rectangle on the vertical crease) and small upright slots left/right (from the square on the horizontal crease).
Left/right slots would have to be horizontal; but the square was on the horizontal crease, so it doubles vertically.
Swaps the roles: tall slots left/right and small slots top/bottom do not come from these punch positions.
Top/bottom slots must be wide (the rectangle doubles across the vertical crease), not small upright ones.

pitfalls: Forgetting that a punch touching a crease doubles in the direction perpendicular to that crease.
cse-2021-1-ga-4.verification: The final pattern has both mirror symmetries (about the vertical and horizontal diameters), as it must after two perpendicular folds.

cse-2021-1-cs-1.approach: CFLs are closed under intersection with a regular language, concatenation and union, but not under complement; $L_1-L_2=L_1\cap\overline{L_2}$ needs $\overline{L_2}$.

steps.body: $L_1\cap L_2$: CFL ∩ regular is CFL (product of PDA and DFA). $L_1\cdot L_2$ and $L_1\cup L_2$: every regular language is CFL, and CFLs are closed under concatenation and union.

steps.title: Difference
steps.body: $L_1-L_2=L_1\cap\overline{L_2}$. With $L_1=\Sigma^*$ this is $\overline{L_2}$, and the complement of a CFL need not be context-free (e.g. $\overline{\{ww\}}$ is CFL but $\{ww\}$ is not). So $L_1-L_2$ is not necessarily CFL.

Concatenation of two CFLs is CFL.

cse-2021-1-cs-12.approach: Emptiness is decidable for DFAs and PDAs; universality is decidable for DFAs but undecidable for PDAs/CFGs.

steps.title: PDA problems
steps.body: Emptiness: convert to CFG and mark generating variables — decidable (C recursive). Universality $L(M)=\Sigma^*$ for PDAs (CFGs) is undecidable (reduction from PCP / computation histories), so D is not recursive.
